children.title: Cycle 34 · Autonomous Systems: Metacognition, Foundational Falsification, and Safety Architectures

detail.title: Autonomous Systems: Metacognition, Foundational Falsification, and Safety Architectures
detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes progress across three active research projects: challenging foundational assumptions in reasoning, adapting CRASH agent architectures for industrial safety, and frameworks for autonomous detection of metacognitive blind spots.

children.title: Analysis of Counterfactual Scoring and Foundational Reasoning Limits

detail.title: Analysis of Counterfactual Scoring and Foundational Reasoning Limits
detail.summary: Recent findings indicate that automated reasoning models encounter irreducible safety failures when foundational premises are tested via counterfactual scoring, suggesting limits in autonomous self-correction.
detail.reason: Revising based on new foundational failure mode evidence.

children.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability

detail.title: Provisional Analysis: CRASH Agent Architecture and Industrial Generalizability
detail.summary: The CRASH agent framework successfully maps heterogeneous safety incidents, but adaptation to heavy industry requires managing noisy, non-standardized data pipelines.
detail.reason: Integrating multi-modal telemetry and agentic framework analysis.

children.title: Frameworks for Autonomous Reasoning Error Attribution

detail.title: Frameworks for Autonomous Reasoning Error Attribution
detail.summary: This research analyzes how autonomous agents might identify reasoning blind spots using anomaly detection, focusing on the gap between intended reasoning and actual trajectory.
detail.reason: Systematizing error logs and metadata to detect internal blind spots.

detail.statement: Automated reasoning models exhibit distinct safety failure profiles under adversarial pressure, preventing universal self-correction strategies.
detail.reason: Recent foundational research confirms that failure attribution is highly context-dependent.
